chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and al-Washa' together, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I had a guest with me, so he desired to eat a citron with honey, so I fed it to him and ate with him. Then I went to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and there was a meal spread before him. He said to me, 'Approach and eat.' I said, 'I have eaten before coming to you a citron with honey, and I still feel its heaviness because I ate a lot of it.' He said, 'O servant, go to the maid and tell her to send us a piece of dry bread from what she dries in the oven.' So it was brought to him, and he said to me, 'Eat from this dry bread, for it digests the citron.' So I ate it. Then I stood up, and it was as if I had not eaten anything.
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam recommend to digest the heaviness of eating citron with honey?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical medical wisdom of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), illustrating the principle of using specific foods to counteract the heaviness or 'thiqal' of others, a concept rooted in humoral theory. It underscores the Imam’s attention to daily physiological well-being, demonstrating that spiritual guidance often encompasses tangible, health-oriented advice for the community. The narrative serves as a testament to the holistic nature of Shia teachings, where physical comfort is seen as conducive to spiritual presence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam and Al Washa altogether from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I had a guest with me, so he desired to eat the Citron with honey, so I fed it to him, and I ate with him. Then I went to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and there was a meal on the table in front of him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Approach, and eat’. So I said, ‘I have eaten before coming to you<sup>asws</sup>, Citron with honey, and I still find its heaviness as I ate a lot from it’. 
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O slave, go to the maid and say to her to send to us the dry pieces of bread from the ones she dries in the oven’. So he came with it, and he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Eat this dry bread for it would digest the Citron’. So I ate it. Then I arose, and it was as if I had not eaten anything’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Washsha’ all from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“There was a guest in my house who liked citron with honey. I served him and I ate with him; then I went to visit abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when the table-spread with food was before him (the Imam). He (the Imam) asked me to come close and eat. I said, ‘I just had citron with honey before coming and I feel heavy because I overate.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘O boy, go to the girl and tell her to send for me pieces of dry loaves of bread of that which she dries up in the oven.’ He brought it and he (the Imam) said to me, ’Eat from this dry bread; it helps one to digests citron.’ I ate it, then left and I felt as if I had not eaten anything.’”
